title: Cardiovascular Disease Multimorbidity
official: Addressing Cardiovascular Disease Multimorbidity in Patients Living With HIV in Nigeria
summary:
This is a hybrid type II effectiveness-implementation trial using a parallel cluster randomized design. Thirty primary healthcare centers (PHCs) in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria, will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to the implementation group (Practice Facilitation \[PF\] + Healthy Lifestyle Counselling, Evidence-Based Protocols, Access to Essential Medicines and Technology, Risk-Based Management, Team-Based Care, and Systems for Monitoring \[HEARTS\] package) or the standard care group (HEARTS only)

The study comprises two phases: an R61 Initiation Phase (Years 1-2) involving adaptation of the HEARTS package guided by the chronic care model, stakeholder engagement, infrastructure development, and pilot testing in 2 PHCs; and an R33 Implementation Phase (Years 3-5) involving the cluster RCT. Once randomized, PHCs will participate in a 12-month intervention period followed by a 6-month post-implementation period.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients are registered to receive care at the eligible and enrolled PHC
* Aged 30 years and older
* Have BP 140-179/90-100 mm Hg
* Have type II diabetes mellitus, defined as either: (a) a new diagnosis based on HbA1c \>6.5% measured at screening; or (b) a prior clinical diagnosis of type II DM documented in the medical record, currently not on antidiabetic treatment. Patients currently receiving antidiabetic medications are excluded.
* Can provide informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* BP \>180/110 mm Hg
* History of chronic kidney disease (eGFR \<35 ml/min)
* History of heart disease
* History of stroke
* Pregnant at time of screening
* Have leg ulcers and/or infection
* Have impaired vision
* Have pins and needles sensation
* Have numbness in hands and feet
* Have proteinuria of 2++
* Acutely ill with high blood sugar (random blood sugar ≥15 mmol/l)\[EM4.1\]
* Unable to provide informed consent
* History of transient ischemic attack (TIA)
